editorial.tldr: On Nov 4 the vLLM project introduced Kinference, an open source inference control plane for vLLM on Kubernetes. A benchmark post comparing it against plain Kubernetes followed a day later.
editorial.whats_new: An InfoQ podcast (Nov 9) places llm-d and vLLM on Kubernetes in the wider distributed-inference conversation, alongside WebAssembly on the backend and TornadoVM for Java on GPUs.
editorial.why_it_matters: Serving LLMs on Kubernetes is moving from generic pod scheduling toward inference-aware control planes (token rate limiting, tenant cost tracking, load balancing), which changes what a platform team builds versus adopts.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run vLLM on Kubernetes, read the Kinference benchmark methodology and rerun it on your own traffic mix before replacing your current routing and rate limiting.

status.detail: Inference-aware Kubernetes tooling is getting launch, benchmark and practitioner coverage, but only one benchmark post exists so far.
